Customer to confirm pricing approval path and PO owner by 2025-02-27
Schedule security deep-dive with Benji and SE for 2025-03-03

meeting_header:
Date: 2025-02-20
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Neill (Redwood SE), Jordan Reyes (Mariner - Procurement), Asha Patel (Mariner - Legal), Benji Kumar (Mariner - Sec Eng), Ellie Wong (Mariner - Finance)
summary: High-level procurement intake to align on MSA/DPA redlines, SLA expectations, KMS/SSO requirements, and billing approval path. Customer has immediate need for sandbox pilot; legal flagged some DPA term questions and KMS/HSM integration. Action items: send redlines, schedule security deep dive, confirm PO owner and pricing approval timeline.
topics: MSA redlines, Data Processing Agreement, SLAs and uptime targets, KMS/HSM integration, SSO/SAML, audit logs and retention, pricing approval process, PO/contracting owner, pilot scope and timeline
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for coming in. This is Maya from Redwood, I'm the account exec. Um, Liam from our side will cover the KMS and technical bits. Jordan, Asha, Benji, Ellie - thanks for making time.
[00:27] Jordan: Yeah thanks. We wanted to use this slot to make sure procurement and legal are aligned before we push to Finance for approval. High level, sandbox pilot, then production if SLAs and DPA line up.
[00:45] Asha: Quick note - legal has a few non-negotiables on data residency and subprocessor lists, and the DPA in the current template has a couple of ambiguous clauses around pseudonymization.
[01:05] Liam: Understood. From a KMS standpoint, we support customer-managed keys with an HSM-backed KMS, or a cloud KMS integration. We can outline key rotation and envelope encryption details.
[01:28] Benji: Right, do you have an architecture diagram for the KMS path? We need to know whether traffic ever leaves our VPC, egress patterns, and log export controls.
[01:47] Liam: I'll share a network diagram - it's used in Private deployments and VPC peering modes. For hosted API, there's optional VPC connector; and we can restrict egress to specific regions.
[02:10] Ellie: On billing, do you have an estimate for sandbox costs versus predictable committed capacity? We need to map that to our budget cycle.
[02:25] Maya: For sandbox, typical cost is minimal - we can give credits - but for production we'd recommend a Dedicated commit to hit predictable SLOs. I'll send a pricing sheet that compares committed vs usage.
[02:45] Jordan: Also procurement wants to know the PO flow - who signs contracts and who's the billing contact.
[02:55] Ellie: Yes, I'll own billing but procurement needs to own the PO routing.
[03:10] Asha: Back to the DPA - our privacy counsel flagged the subprocessors section and cross-border transfer language. We usually require SCCs or equivalent mechanisms.
[03:30] Maya: We include SCCs where required and have an EU data residency option. We'll highlight transfer mechanisms in the DPA redline.
[03:50] Speaker 3: (background) sorry, can you repeat the SCCs bit?
[03:55] Asha: Standard Contractual Clauses - we need to ensure they're active for EU data.
[04:12] Liam: For audit logs, we can store logs in customer-owned S3 or ship to their SIEM; retention policies are configurable per account. Does that meet your compliance needs?
[04:30] Benji: Potentially. We need proofs: can you provide SOC-2 Type II report and, ideally, penetration test summary?
[04:45] Maya: Yes, we have SOC 2 and pen test reports — we'll share redacted copies through the secure portal.
[04:58] Jordan: On SLAs, our bar for production is 99.9% availability and P95 latency under our defined request shapes. How does Redwood approach SLA guarantees and credits?
[05:17] Liam: We have SLA tiers — Hosted has best-effort with performance targets, Dedicated has formal uptime SLA and latency SLOs for pinned capacity. Credits are applied per contract terms; we can propose language in the MSA.
[05:36] Asha: In our past experiences, vague 'best-effort' language doesn't fly. We will need explicit SLOs tied to credits for production. For sandbox it's ok to be lower.
[05:50] Maya: That's fair. We'll draft suggested SLA clauses for Dedicated and outline fallback policies if capacity is constrained.
[06:05] Jordan: Procurement will also check indemnity and liability caps. We usually push for a cap at 1x annual fees for SaaS but exceptions for data breaches sometimes apply.
[06:20] Asha: Also looking at DPA breach notification timelines — we require 72 hours for high-severity incidents.
[06:33] Liam: Our incident response includes 72-hour notification and postmortem sharing; for Private deployments we can offer deeper logging.
[06:48] Maya: On the redlines, are there particular MSA clauses that are likely showstoppers?
[06:55] Asha: Termination for convenience with 60 days notice, liability cap, and data transfer clauses are the big three. Also, audit rights — we need clarity on how audits occur without exposing other customers.
[07:15] Liam: For audits, we can provide SOC 2 plus scoped logs; for in-depth audits on Private deployments we support onsite or virtual audit with NDAs.
[07:35] Ellie: Pricing again — if we take Dedicated, what's the commit period? 12 months? 24?
[07:45] Maya: Standard is 12 months, annual billing; we can discuss multi-year discounts if you lock capacity.
[07:58] Jordan: Timeline-wise, procurement aims to have vendor approved by end of March so we can onboard in Q2. Does that align?
[08:10] Maya: Yes, that's reasonable. We'll aim to get MSA/DPA to you for review within a week.
[08:20] Speaker 3: (unclear) can we get an example of the SLA table?
[08:25] Liam: I'll attach the SLA table to the follow-up email and walk through metrics.
[08:40] Asha: One more legal note: any third-party subprocessors list needs update window - we prefer 30 days' notice for onboarding new subprocessors.
[08:52] Maya: Noted. We can add a 30-day notice clause for subprocessor changes.
[09:05] Benji: For the KMS flow, does Redwood ever hold plaintext keys or raw customer secrets?
[09:15] Liam: No, we use envelope encryption; customer master keys never leave the KMS. We can sign an operational attestation describing key handling.
[09:30] Benji: Great. Also curious about egress — will model inference flow cause PHI to transit outside the region for model weights hosting?
[09:42] Maya: For Private deployments weights stay in-customer VPC. For hosted models, we can pin models to region, and we offer a private deployment option if you need full control.
[09:58] Ellie: Any escrow for models or critical IP if provider goes out of business? Procurement sometimes requires an escrow for long contracts.
[10:10] Maya: We don't currently offer code escrow for model weights but we can discuss contractual continuity plans and data export guarantees.
[10:25] Jordan: Ok, next - approval path. I need a one-pager for our approvers summarizing the risk, costs, mitigations. Can Redwood produce that?
[10:35] Maya: Yes, we'll prepare a vendor brief that summarizes SLA, DPA highlights, security posture, and pricing scenarios.
[10:48] Asha: Are you comfortable with us redlining your DPA? We'll track changes and send them back.
[10:55] Maya: Absolutely, we expect redlines. We'll try to accommodate standard enterprise asks where possible; if there's major divergence we'll flag it for executive review.
[11:10] Liam: I'll also assemble the technical appendix with KMS, SSO/SAML flows, network diagrams, and SIEM integration instructions.
[11:25] Benji: For SSO we require SAML 2.0 and SCIM for user provisioning. Do you support SCIM?
[11:35] Liam: Yes, SCIM provisioning is supported for user sync, and SAML 2.0 is available for SSO. We also support OIDC for some clients.
[11:50] Ellie: For billing - are invoices monthly or can you do net-30 payment terms?
[11:58] Maya: Standard is monthly invoicing with net-30; for large committed deals we can negotiate payment schedules.
[12:10] Jordan: Regarding subprocessors, can you provide a current list and a process for notifying us?
[12:18] Maya: Yes - we'll attach the current subprocessor list and propose a 30-day notice clause as discussed.
[12:30] Asha: On the liability cap, are you open to carving out data breach exceptions?
[12:38] Maya: We'll propose standard carve-outs for security incidents; exact liability language we'll propose in tracked redlines.
[12:50] Speaker 3: (inaudible)
[12:55] Liam: Quick operational question - for pilot evals, what's the expected throughput? We need token estimates to size the sandbox.
[13:08] Jordan: For pilot it's light - maybe a few hundred concurrent requests daily, but production may scale to thousands.
[13:18] Liam: Okay that'll be fine. For sandbox we'll allocate small containers; for production we can discuss dedicated GPU pools.
[13:30] Ellie: One more on finance - how do you handle tax and cross-border billing?
[13:40] Maya: We issue invoices from our US entity by default; for other jurisdictions we can route through partners or local entities in certain cases. We'll flag tax considerations in the brief.
[13:55] Asha: Any SOC 2 scope details? Do your pen tests include network layer and app layer?
[14:05] Liam: Pen test summary includes app layer and selected infra components; SOC 2 covers data handling controls. We'll include the date scopes of the reports.
[14:20] Jordan: Ok let's walk through a hypothetical MSA redline exchange. We send redlines, Redwood accepts some, rejects others, then exec escalation if needed?
[14:35] Maya: Yes that's our usual flow. Small redline items we handle at AE/GC level; major liability or IP items go to legal leadership. We'll flag items that need escalation.
[14:50] Asha: For DPA retention - we require deletion confirmation within 30 days of termination. Is that workable?
[14:58] Liam: We can confirm deletion procedures and provide a certificate of deletion for customer-owned storage options.
[15:10] Benji: Another question — do you have an SLA for data durability of logs and backups?
[15:22] Liam: Durability typically follows cloud provider guarantees; we can outline retention and redundancy in the appendix.
[15:35] Maya: Quick moment - I'll recap actions at the end, but any other blockers we haven't raised?
[15:45] Jordan: From procurement side, main blockers are pricing approval and PO owner confirmation.
[15:53] Ellie: From finance, confirm who will be signatory and the billing entity.
[16:02] Asha: From legal, redlines and subprocessors process.
[16:10] Benji: Security needs the technical appendix and SOC-2/pen tests.
[16:18] Maya: Great. We'll get a vendor brief and redlines out. Liam will produce the tech appendix and SLA table.
[16:30] Liam: I'll also include a short KMS attestation and sample network diagram.
[16:40] Jordan: Can we do the security deep-dive on March 3rd, as Maya suggested?
[16:46] Maya: Yes let's tentatively schedule March 3rd at 10am PT — I'll send the invite.
[17:00] Speaker 3: (overlap) thanks
[17:05] Asha: One more question about escrow - is there a customer-friendly continuity plan?
[17:15] Maya: We can draft continuity language: expedited data export, support transition assistance, and assistance with model rehosting where feasible. We'll mark that for legal.
[17:30] Ellie: Also need a breakdown of pilot deliverables and success metrics so we can judge the pilot.
[17:40] Maya: We'll include pilot scope and success criteria in the vendor brief.
[17:50] Jordan: Ok, that covers the major points. Thanks all.
[18:00] Maya: Thanks everyone — I'll send the follow-up with attachments.
[18:06] Transcript ends (system note: recording clipped at several spots; some speaker labels may be generic)
